title: Basic Conditional Structures
lede: Use إذا for real, expected and repeated conditions, and لو for hypothetical or counterfactual alternatives, with coherent result clauses.

items.feedback: إذا commonly presents a real, expected or repeated condition.
لو introduces an unreal or imagined condition.

items.prompt: Which often means “when” as well as “if”?
items.feedback: إذا can introduce an expected future or recurring event.
The result may be an instruction; فـ can link it clearly.

items.prompt: Complete: لَوْ كُنْتُ غَنِيًّا، ___ حَوْلَ الْعَالَمِ.
items.feedback: لـ often marks the result of لو.

options: Use basic condition-result patterns accurately in meaningful contexts.
Treat إذا and لو as identical.
items.feedback: Functional contrast is the IGCSE priority.

can clearly introduce the result clause

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَسْتَعْمِلُ الشَّرْطَ؟
Conditionals connect an action to its consequence and let learners give advice, explain outcomes and imagine alternatives.
### Core
Use basic إذا condition-result sentences.
### Develop
Contrast likely إذا with hypothetical لو and use varied results.
### Stretch
Recognise formal إنْ and counterfactual patterns as Stretch.
[callout] Communication target: Extend a simple answer with a realistic consequence and a hypothetical alternative.
## Diagnostic start
Decide whether each condition is real or imagined.
## إِذَا and لَوْ: real versus imagined
The choice changes how the speaker presents the condition.

TABLE: Connector | Core meaning | Model | Communicative use // إِذَا | if / when; real, expected or repeated | إِذَا دَرَسْتَ، سَتَنْجَحُ. | advice, routines, likely outcomes // لَوْ | if; imagined, unlikely or contrary to fact | لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ، لَسَافَرْتُ. | dreams, hypotheses, regrets // إِنْ (Stretch) | if; formal open condition | إِنْ تَجْتَهِدْ تَنْجَحْ. | formal conditional pattern
[callout] Meaning contrast: إِذَا presents the condition as realistic or expected. لَوْ opens an imagined alternative.
## Functional patterns with إِذَا
Use a small set of reliable condition-result frames.
### Pattern A: past-form verbs, future/expected meaning
إِذَا وَصَلْتَ، سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكَ.
The past form after إذا does not necessarily refer to past time.
### Pattern B: completed-form condition with a habitual result
إِذَا شَعَرْتُ بِالتَّعَبِ، أَنَامُ مُبَكِّرًا.
The past-form condition can introduce what regularly happens whenever the condition is met.
### Pattern C: instruction result
إِذَا احْتَجْتَ إِلَى مُسَاعَدَةٍ، فَاسْأَلْنِي.
### Pattern D: nominal result
إِذَا كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا، فَالرِّحْلَةُ مُمْتِعَةٌ.
[callout/warning] Avoid rigid English tense transfer. Arabic often uses a past form after إذا for a future expected event: إِذَا وَصَلْتَ = when/if you arrive.
## Hypotheses with لَوْ
Use لو to imagine alternatives, express wishes and reflect on unreal past possibilities.

TABLE: Hypothetical frame | Model | Meaning // لَوْ + كَانَ | لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي مَالٌ، لَاشْتَرَيْتُ سَيَّارَةً. | If I had money, I would buy a car. // لَوْ + كُنْتُ | لَوْ كُنْتُ مُدِيرًا، لَغَيَّرْتُ الْقَوَاعِدَ. | If I were a manager… // لَوْ + past event | لَوْ دَرَسْتُ أَكْثَرَ، لَنَجَحْتُ. | If I had studied more, I would have succeeded. // لَوْلَا (Stretch) | لَوْلَا الْمَطَرُ، لَخَرَجْنَا. | If it were not for the rain…
[callout] Result marker: The لَـ on لَسَافَرْتُ، لَاشْتَرَيْتُ is a common signal of the result clause after لَوْ .
## Conditionals extend answers
A conditional adds cause, consequence, advice, imagination or reflection to simple statements.

[callout] Speaking ladder: fact → likely condition → hypothetical extension. أُحِبُّ السَّفَرَ. إِذَا سَافَرْتُ فِي الصَّيْفِ، سَأَزُورُ الْمَغْرِبَ. وَلَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ أَطْوَلُ، لَزُرْتُ بِلَادًا أُخْرَى.

TABLE: Topic | Likely frame with إذا | Hypothetical frame with لو // study | إِذَا دَرَسْتُ بِجِدٍّ، سَأَنْجَحُ. | لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ أَكْثَرُ، لَدَرَسْتُ لُغَةً أُخْرَى. // travel | إِذَا سَافَرْنَا، سَنَسْتَعْمِلُ الْقِطَارَ. | لَوْ كُنْتُ غَنِيًّا، لَسَافَرْتُ حَوْلَ الْعَالَمِ. // environment | إِذَا قَلَّلْنَا النُّفَايَاتِ، سَنَحْمِي الْبِيئَةَ. | لَوْ كَانَتِ الطَّاقَةُ النَّظِيفَةُ أَرْخَصَ، لَاسْتَعْمَلَهَا الْجَمِيعُ.
## Conditional misconception clinic
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
### إذا time
✗ إِذَا وَصَلْتَ أَمْسِ، سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكَ غَدًا دون سياق
✓ إِذَا وَصَلْتَ غَدًا، فَاتَّصِلْ بِي
Keep the condition and result time relationship coherent.
### Future marker inside condition
✗ إِذَا سَوْفَ تَدْرُسُ، سَتَنْجَحُ
✓ إِذَا دَرَسْتَ، سَتَنْجَحُ
A compact standard frame uses past-form condition plus future result.
### لو versus إذا
✗ لَوْ شَعَرْتُ بِالْجُوعِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، لَأَكَلْتُ
✓ إِذَا شَعَرْتُ بِالْجُوعِ، آكُلُ
Routine/repeated relation uses إذا.
### Result lam
✗ لَوْ كُنْتُ غَنِيًّا، سَافَرْتُ حَوْلَ الْعَالَمِ
✓ لَوْ كُنْتُ غَنِيًّا، لَسَافَرْتُ حَوْلَ الْعَالَمِ
The lam clearly signals the hypothetical result.
## Replayable conditional game
Match connector, condition and result.
## Apply the grammar across skills
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
### 📖 Reading workshop
Read advice posts and distinguish likely conditions from imagined alternatives. Identify the result in each sentence.
### 🎧 Listening workshop
Listen to eight condition-result pairs and decide whether the speaker expects the condition or is imagining it.
### 🗣️ Speaking workshop
Answer a topic question, then add one إذا consequence and one لو hypothetical extension.
### 🛠️ Editing workshop
Repair conditional sentences with incoherent time frames, mixed connectors and missing result markers.
### ✍️ Integrated production task
Write 120–140 words giving advice about study, health or the environment. Include three realistic إذا conditions and two hypothetical لو extensions.

[callout] Model: إِذَا نَظَّمْتَ وَقْتَكَ، سَتُكْمِلُ وَاجِبَاتِكَ بِسُهُولَةٍ. وَإِذَا شَعَرْتَ بِالتَّعَبِ، فَاسْتَرِحْ قَلِيلًا. وَلَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي يَوْمٌ إِضَافِيٌّ، لَخَصَّصْتُهُ لِلْمُرَاجَعَةِ.
[callout] Success checklist: Use a future result, an imperative result, a nominal result and at least one لو + كان/كنت frame.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Draw two columns headed “real/expected” and “imagined”. Draft each condition in the correct column before writing the final response.
## Final mastery check
Choose and build basic functional conditionals.
### Lesson mastery summary
- use إذا for real, expected and recurring conditions;
- use لو for imagined and counterfactual conditions;
- build coherent future, command and nominal results;
- extend speaking and writing with cause-and-consequence relationships.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
